title: Activation traffic lane and metrics journal
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a tactical journal for the next product activation window focused on controlled traffic shifts, KPI instrumentation, and immediate rollback criteria. Audience: product ops, release engineering, SRE on-call, and launch owners. Treat this as the single source notebook during the 72-hour activation period.

High-level activation objective:
- Ramp a new model routing policy and a lightweight caching optimization for hosted API routes /v1/generate and /v1/chat with minimal user-visible regressions while reducing per-token cost on steady-state traffic by ~12% for the target cohort.

Primary success metrics (Day 0 baseline vs target by Day 14):
- Error rate (5xx + 4xx unexpected) for target routes: baseline 0.32% -> target <= 0.5% (temporary tolerance during canary), long-term <= 0.2%
- Median latency (p50) for short sequences (<128 tokens): baseline 86ms -> target <= 95ms
- 95th percentile latency (p95): baseline 420ms -> target <= 520ms
- Token cost per 1k tokens for target model family: baseline $0.42 -> target <= $0.37 (12% reduction)
- Quality regressions (automated eval set pass rate): baseline 96% -> target >= 94% (we allow up to 2 point drop during canary but require reconciliation plan)
- Adoption signal: percent of routed traffic honored by new policy: Day 3 >= 10%, Day 7 >= 40%, Day 14 >= 85%

Activation lanes (traffic slices and rules):
- Canary lane A (internal alpha): 1% of traffic, users with flagged accounts = internal-emails domain. Owner: Mateo.
- Canary lane B (partner beta): 5% of traffic, partners labeled in partner-routing tag. Owner: Priya.
- Ramp lane (gradual public): incrementally increase by 5–10% every 24 hours if safety checks pass. Owner: Sofia.
- Safety fallback lane: instant fallback to previous routing policy on any lane if rollback criteria met. Owner on-call SRE.

Daily checkpoints and owner responsibilities:
- Pre-activation (T-48 to T-2): confirm metric dashboards wired (SLOs, error streams, cost), smoke test routing rules in staging (release eng), update release notes and customer comms draft (product ops).
- Activation start (T0): announce start in #prod-ops and #sre-alerts with ticket link, snapshot key dashboards, wire up logs to ephemeral short retention channel for triage (Sofia).
- Hourly snapshot cadence (first 6 hours): collect error rate, p50/p95, cost delta, eval-set automated run, user-visible errors. Owner collects and posts in ticket.
- 3-hour deep review (T+3): cross-team check for anomalies; decide whether to continue ramp. Participants: product ops, release eng, SRE, data quality.
- Daily review (end of day): compile day summary, escalation notes, and recommendations for next step.

Preflight checklist (must be green before T0):
- [ ] Signing: Exec sponsor confirmed (email thread attached).
- [ ] Metrics: dashboards exist and show pre-activation baseline for last 7 days.
- [ ] Instrumentation: synthetic eval runner configured and sanity tests pass in staging and canary infra.
- [ ] Alerts: temporary threshold alerts created for p95 latency, error spike, and quality regression.
- [ ] Rollback script: verified in staging; one-button revert tested by release eng.
- [ ] Customer comms: FAQ and support playbook drafted and reviewed by CS.
- [ ] Compliance: privacy checklist for cache telemetry signed off by security.

Rollback and go/no-go criteria (automated and manual):
Automated immediate rollback triggers (any lane):
- Error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5 minutes
- p95 latency > 1500ms sustained for 5 minutes
- Automated eval run shows quality drop > 6 points vs baseline
Manual escalation triggers (requires cross-team review):
- Unexpected backend resource exhaustion (GPU OOMs, retry storms)
- Customer escalations with reproducible failures from production samples
- Cost deviation > 40% from prediction for the active lane

Risk register and mitigations (top 6):
- Risk: Eval set lacks representative edge cases. Mitigation: run ad-hoc prompt sets from partner beta, increase sampling frequency, revert if quality delta exceeds tolerance. Owner: Arjun.
- Risk: Traffic spike causes autoscaler thrash. Mitigation: pre-warm dedicated capacity for first 2 hours, tuning autoscale cooldown longer. Owner: Release Engineering.
- Risk: Incorrect routing config exposure. Mitigation: feature-flag gating + circuit breaker. Owner: Platform Eng.

Operational runbook snippets (quick actions):
- If latency spike observed: check model queue lengths -> inspect batch size, KV cache hit rate -> temporarily reduce concurrency for target pool -> throttle new lane increments.
- If quality regression flagged: snapshot last 100 prompts -> run evaluation harness locally -> compare top-k outputs with golden set -> if regression reproducible, trigger rollback and open ticket with model-onboarding.
- If cost anomaly: confirm billing attribution tags -> inspect quantization toggles and cache hit ratio -> pause ramp if cost per token exceeds threshold.

Communication templates (to post in Slack ticket channel):
- T0 announcement template: "Starting activation window for routing-policy X at HH:MM. Canary A=1%, B=5%. Primary owners: Sofia, Mateo, Priya. Dashboards: <link>. Rollback instructions pinned. Expect hourly snapshots first 6 hours."
- Rollback notification template: "Initiating immediate rollback for routing-policy X at HH:MM due to [reason]. Reverting to policy Y. Notifying incident channel and CS. Post-mortem ticket: <JIRA>"

Metrics capture table (fields to include in hourly snapshot):
- timestamp, lane, percent_traffic, error_rate, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_served, cost_per_1k_tokens, eval_pass_rate, notable_logs_count

Post-activation stabilization plan (Day 1–30):
- Day 1-3: Stop increases, monitor stability and customer signals, prioritize any hot fixes.
- Day 4-7: Gradual traffic increase to final target if metrics stable. Confirm cost targets and schedule optimization sweep.
- Day 7-14: Remove temporary alert thresholds and revert to long-term SLOs. Run expanded quality eval across 3 production slices.
- Day 15-30: Run performance tuning job for kernel selection and batching based on observed seq length distribution; publish short findings doc.

Open questions to resolve before final sign-off:
- Should we include a soft quota throttle for partner beta to cap downstream cost exposure? Owner: Priya.
- Do we need to schedule a follow-up retro with CS to capture edge-case tickets within 7 days? Owner: Sofia.

Notes and attachments reference list:
- linked artifacts above include deploy scripts and JIRA. Additional Confluence playbook section: "activation-conduct" (see linked_artifacts entry).
- Attach worklog: staging-smoke.log, canary-eval-2025-11-18.csv, cost-model-simulation-v2.xlsx

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Mateo: finalize internal canary list and confirm partner readiness (by T-24).
- Priya: prepare partner-facing release notes and support doc (by T-24).
- Arjun: run one more offline eval sweep with partner prompts and post summary (by T-12).
- Sofia: create activation ticket, schedule T0 announcement, and ensure SRE on-call rota aligned (by T-6).

Revision history:
- 2025-11-18 Sofia Chen: initial draft and metric targets
- 2025-12-02 Arjun Patel: added risk mitigations and operational snippets
- 2026-02-10 Priya Natarajan: updated ramp cadence and final preflight checklist items

End of journal entry.
